sources.title: ATO: Concessional contributions cap
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026 (page last updated 2 July 2026): Concessional cap $32,500 from 1 July 2026; $30,000 from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2026. Carry-forward needs a total super balance under $500,000 at 30 June of the previous year; unused amounts from up to 5 previous years, starting from 2018-19, applied oldest first and expiring after 5 years. Excess concessional contributions are assessable with a 15% offset; up to 85% can be released; the election window is 60 days (available online up to 120 days); unreleased excess counts as non-concessional.

sources.title: ATO: Non-concessional contributions cap
sources.fact: Reviewed by Ryan Duguid on 24 September 2026 (page last updated 7 May 2026): Non-concessional cap $130,000 for 2026-27 ($120,000 for 2024-25 and 2025-26). Nil cap where total super balance at the end of the previous year is at or above the general transfer balance cap ($2.1 million from 2026-27). Bring-forward for 2026-27: under $1.84 million, $390,000 over 3 years; $1.84 million to under $1.97 million, $260,000 over 2 years; $1.97 million to under $2.1 million, $130,000 with no bring-forward. Available if under 75 at any time in the year.
